items.headline: XIAOMI REPORTS TONIGHT — results have NOT landed. Filing after the HK close, investor call 19:30 Beijing
items.summary: Clock verified against the machine: as of 08:30 SGT Tuesday 18 August, Xiaomi's H1/Q2 results are NOT out. Treat any figure circulating now as an estimate, not an actual. PRIMARY SOURCE, quoted verbatim from the HKEX board-meeting filing dated 17 July 2026: a Board meeting 'will be held on August 18, 2026 (Tuesday)' for 'considering and approving the unaudited consolidated interim results of the Company and its subsidiaries for the six months ended June 30, 2026, and considering the payment of an interim dividend, if any.' Signed Lei Jun, Chairman. TIMING CORRECTED: the 19:30 Beijing slot is the investor conference call; the results filing itself lands after the HK close. PRICE CONTEXT from the deterministic feed: Xiaomi fell four consecutive sessions into the print (26.66 → 26.36 → 25.88 → 25.62) before recovering 1.01% Monday to HK$25.88.
items.actionable: Your 26,662 shares report tonight AFTER the close, so today's HK session trades blind and the gap risk is Wednesday's open. Three things to read first when it lands: whether an interim dividend is actually declared — the filing says only 'if any', and a dividend alongside a sharp profit decline would be a genuine surprise; the EV segment's margin trajectory; and whether the smartphone share story survives. Tencent's precedent is the caution: it de-risked into its print, then fell 4.46% on the day.

items.headline: GOLD BROKE OUT AND HELD IT — new high 4,486.50, closed 4,479.50 (+2.26%). After three failed attempts, this one stuck
items.summary: From the deterministic price feed: gold front-month closed 4,479.50, up 2.26%, with a session high of 4,486.50. THE PATTERN BREAK IS THE POINT. The three preceding attempts all faded — 12 Aug made 4,434.00 and closed 4,408.90; 13 Aug made 4,445.00 and closed 4,363.60, giving the whole move back; 14 Aug made 4,397.10. Monday cleared the prior 4,445 peak and closed within $7 of its high. THE DRIVER IS MONETARY, NOT REAL-YIELD: September hike odds fell to roughly one-in-three from nearly 50%, and the dollar index slipped below 100 toward two-month lows. Confirmed drivers on a dated page: fading hike expectations, dimmed prospects for a US-Iran agreement, Trump's refusal to extend the interim deal, and continued central-bank purchases, particularly from China. CORRECTION APPLIED IN VERIFICATION: a claim that the University of Michigan release 'explicitly attributed' its drop to the Iran war lifting fuel and food prices was DELETED — the release says no such thing; its only Iran reference is that Republican sentiment sits 19% below pre-conflict readings.
items.actionable: The thing to notice is that gold made this high while the long end sat at multi-year highs — normally hostile. That says the bid is debasement and haven demand rather than falling real rates, which is a more durable engine but also a more fragile one: it unwinds fast if US-Iran talks resume. This is the first genuinely constructive session for the metals complex in a week.

items.headline: OIL'S $91 BREAKOUT IS A REAL CATALYST: the US-Iran MOU formally expired Monday, Trump declined to extend, and Tehran went 'fully offensive' on Hormuz
items.summary: Brent settled 91.11 (+2.93%) with a 91.43 high — a clean break above the prior range top of 90.07. WTI 84.95 (+3.09%). THE CATALYST, verified at primary sources: an IntelBrief dated 17 Aug states that 'the defunct June U.S.-Iran Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) formally expires on Monday.' Trump's refusal to extend is independently corroborated on a second dated page. A Reuters report dated 17 Aug, sourced to a senior Iranian official speaking Monday, carries the shift: Iranian entities 'must be prepared to escalate tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and wider region,' with a 'timely and precise' military attack to break the naval blockade if talks collapse, and 'within the short period of a few weeks set by Iran, all the agreement's provisions must be implemented by the U.S.' TWO THINGS DELETED IN VERIFICATION, both of which would have overstated the case: the vessel-transit collapse story (five vessels Saturday, none Sunday) came only from a page returning HTTP 403 and is CONTRADICTED by independent maritime tracking showing 12 transits in the 24 hours of 16 Aug; and Trump's most inflammatory quote is timestamped 07:44 ET, a morning remark, not an afternoon escalation.
items.actionable: The oil sleeve is now long a live escalation rather than a stalemate, with a dated several-week Iranian ultimatum as the clock. But size to the diplomatic track, NOT to a supply outage: the physical-disruption story failed verification and independent tracking contradicts it. The second-order effect matters more for the rest of the book — this same oil move is the named driver behind the long end and the September hike tail, which is the direct threat to the levered silver.

items.headline: THE OTHER SIDE OF IT: the 10Y rose past 4.7% and the 30Y sits above 5.2%, its highest since 2007 — the long end still will not rally
items.summary: Commentary dated 17 Aug: 'The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note rose past 4.7% on Monday, not far from the 19-month high of 4.75% tested last week as lingering concerns of inflation and increasing credit supply extended the aversion to bonds in the long end of the curve.' FALSE PRECISION STRIPPED IN VERIFICATION: specific closes of 10Y 4.724% and 30Y 5.311%, and the 'highest since June 2007 / 19-year high' framing, rested solely on a page returning HTTP 403 and are NOT published. What is verified is the direction and the rough level. Named drivers include record AI-related bond issuance adding supply, alongside the inflation impulse from oil. CONTEXT from our own verified series: this follows a week in which an in-line CPI and a soft PPI produced ZERO net duration relief, with the 10Y round-tripping to exactly 4.68%.
items.actionable: This is the single most important line for the book's largest risk. A 1.6x margin-levered silver position is short duration and short real rates by construction, and a 30Y at post-2007 highs with a live one-in-three September hike tail is precisely the adverse scenario — driven by the very oil move that is helping the energy sleeve. The two positions are now hedging each other by accident rather than design. It also keeps structural pressure on Keppel REIT and the Mapletrees.

items.headline: Silver posted its best close of the run (66.065, +1.66%) but STILL a lower high — and there is no silver-specific driver behind it
items.summary: From the deterministic feed: silver front-month closed 66.065, its best close of the sequence, but its 66.145 session high remains BELOW the 66.650 high of 12 August. So the fade pattern broke while the ceiling did not. THE NEGATIVE FINDING IS THE VALUE HERE, and it was confirmed rather than merely unrefuted: the only dated commentary attributes the move ENTIRELY to macro — tame inflation, weak consumer sentiment, soft retail sales, reduced Fed hike expectations, plus Middle East risk. It contains NO silver-specific catalyst: no squeeze, no inventory event, no industrial-demand news. The gold/silver ratio widened to 67.8, meaning silver UNDERPERFORMED gold on a strong day for both.
items.actionable: Do not attribute Monday to a physical squeeze — there is no dated evidence for one, and the widening ratio argues against it. Silver is trading as a high-beta gold proxy and sits in a genuine crosscurrent: the debasement bid helps it, while the same weak-consumer data driving that bid also softens industrial demand. At 1.6x, Monday was worth about +2.66% on the position. The level that still matters is 66.65; until it clears, this remains a lower high.

items.headline: The miners re-coupled to the metal — which retrospectively marks Thursday's breakdown as positioning, not a fundamental break
items.summary: From the deterministic feed: GDX +2.13%, Newmont +2.18%, Barrick +3.16%, Pan American +1.46%, SILJ +0.13%, against gold +2.26%. Straightforward beta. The notable thing is the ABSENCE of a repeat of Thursday 13 August, when the complex fell 2-3x the metal (GDX -2.96%, Newmont -3.10%, Pan American -9.70%) on a day gold fell only 1.03% and the S&P closed at a record. No company or sector announcement dated Monday explains the move. FIGURES GUTTED IN VERIFICATION — worth stating because it is most of what made the original item feel informative: a set of Newmont Q2 numbers ($4,414/oz realised, $1,621 AISC, $2.2bn FCF) is NOT published here because the company results URL returned HTTP 404 and no primary source could be opened. The Nevada Gold Mines transaction is real but dated 10 August, NOT Monday: Barrick transfers Fourmile into the joint venture, Newmont transfers Mike and Fiberline and pays Barrick $1.95bn.
items.actionable: Treat Monday as evidence that the 13 August dislocation was positioning rather than a fundamental break — the complex re-coupled on the first strong gold day. That read is safe precisely because it rests on price behaviour rather than on earnings figures, which is fortunate given how few of those survived checking. Do not size on the unverified Newmont numbers.

items.headline: CHINA MISSED ON ALL FOUR headline measures — and Hong Kong rallied 1.34% anyway, with the data landing an hour before the close
items.summary: Released Monday 15:00 Beijing, an hour before the HK close. ACTUALS vs consensus, all four worse: industrial production 4.5% y/y (cons. 5.0%, June 5.3%); retail sales 0.6% y/y (cons. 1.5%, June 1.0%); fixed-asset investment -6.7% ytd y/y (cons. -6.2%, steepening from -5.7%, the lowest since April 2020); surveyed urban unemployment 5.2% (cons. 5.1%, June 5.0%). Confirmed on the NBS release index, on an ING economist note and on a Reuters wire, all stamped 2026-08-17. CONSENSUS CAVEAT: the consensus set is source-dependent — ING and Reuters use 5.0/1.5/-6.2, which is what is reported here; another outlet used slightly different figures. THIS IS THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE MISS: Friday's July net new yuan loans CONTRACTED CNY 340bn, the largest monthly contraction on record, against expectations of a CNY 45bn increase, with outstanding loan growth at a record-low 5.1% y/y.
items.actionable: The striking thing is what the market did with it: Hong Kong closed UP 1.34% on a day every major China macro print missed, with the data in hand an hour before the close. Semiconductors set the tape, not macro. That tells you the HK bid is currently an AI-hardware story running independently of the domestic economy — which is good for your SMIC and Xiaomi exposure and bad as a reason to own China breadth. Two consecutive misses also raise the odds of stimulus; the 1-year and 5-year Loan Prime Rates are set Thursday.

items.headline: Hang Seng 25,453.23 (+1.34%) snapped a four-session losing streak; STI 5,768.46 (+0.43%) closed exactly on its high after opening down 0.86%
items.summary: VERIFIED ON THREE INDEPENDENT PAGES EACH — these are the two index levels our price feed could not supply, though it had every constituent. Hang Seng 25,453.23, +336.38 points, +1.34%, snapping a four-session losing streak; Hang Seng Tech +1.58% (+74.41) to 4,782.03; turnover HK$210.77bn. STI 5,768.46, +0.43%, having opened 0.86% lower and closed exactly on its session high. DATA-QUALITY FLAG, confirmed and narrowed: one outlet printed '24,453' alongside '+336 points' and '+1.34%' — arithmetically impossible, since 25,453.23 - 336.38 = 25,116.85, which is exactly Friday's verified close, and 336.38/25,116.85 = 1.34%. The dropped digit is real and 25,453.23 is correct.
items.actionable: Both indices reversed intraday weakness to close strong, and the STI closing precisely on its high after a down open is the kind of tape that usually reflects real buying rather than short-covering. Hong Kong entering Tuesday off a four-session low with a 1.34% reversal is a better setup for Xiaomi's print tonight than the tape looked on Friday.

items.headline: SMIC +6.14% to HK$75.15 is a PRICE-HIKE story, not a beat story — and Monday was only the SECOND post-results session
items.summary: OFF-BY-ONE CORRECTED: Q2 results were announced 13 August after the HK close, making Friday 14 August the FIRST post-results session and Monday the SECOND — not the third, as originally filed. Five-day gain roughly 13.6%. Q2 ACTUALS confirmed: revenue US$3.006bn (+20.0% q/q, +36.1% y/y); gross profit US$760.6m against US$503.6m in Q1 (+51.0%); gross margin 25.3% against 20.1% (+5.2pp); capacity utilisation 93.7% against 93.1%. GUIDANCE BEAT CONFIRMED: SMIC had guided in May to 14-16% sequential revenue growth and a 20-22% gross margin, and delivered +20.0% and 25.3% — clear of both. Q3 guidance takes gross margin up another 1-3pp on wafers already contracted at higher prices.
items.actionable: The re-rating runs on pricing power and utilisation near 94%, with Q3 margin guided higher on wafers ALREADY contracted at new prices — that is a forward margin lever, not a one-off beat, which is why the move is extending rather than fading. The corrected session count matters for how much is already in the price: Monday was the second reaction session, so this is early rather than late. SMIC remains the one HK holding where the news flow is unambiguously working.

items.headline: Singapore NODX +24.2% y/y on a 112% electronics surge — the AI trade is now visibly in the trade data
items.summary: Enterprise Singapore released July external trade Monday 17 August. Non-oil domestic exports rose 24.2% y/y, accelerating from an upwardly revised 20.8% in June and a fourth consecutive month above 20%. THE COMPOSITION IS EXTRAORDINARY: electronic NODX +112% y/y (after +105.1% in June, so still accelerating), while non-electronic NODX FELL 2.3%, led lower by pharmaceuticals off a high base, then petrochemicals and food preparations. Within electronics the AI fingerprint is explicit: disk media +339.1% (+S$1.6bn) and integrated circuits +84.5% (+S$1.4bn). Non-oil re-exports +51.3%, with electronics re-exports +75.2%. Year-to-date NODX through July +19.4%. Verified on two independently opened pages, both stamped 2026-08-17.
items.actionable: Same underlying driver as SMIC: AI hardware demand. Note the K-shape printed in two economies on the same day — Singapore's export engine and China's high-tech output are booming while their domestic and traditional sectors contract. Supportive for the SGX bank sleeve, which is levered to trade finance and regional growth; DBS rose 1.79% Monday. It does nothing for the REIT sleeve, which remains a duration story.

items.headline: CORRECTION to our own Fed framing: the September debate is HOLD vs HIKE — three officials already voted for a hike in July, and hike odds sit at 35.3%
items.summary: Verified against the Fed's own 29 July 2026 release: the FOMC held at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, and 'Voting against the monetary policy action were Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie K. Logan, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting' — THREE dissents, all for a HIKE. The statement's inflation language, verbatim: inflation 'remains elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy.' WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE DASHBOARD: our '~69% hold' phrasing reads naturally as hold-versus-CUT. It is not. There is no cut in the distribution. Hike odds stood at 35.3% after Monday's close, down from nearly 50%.
items.actionable: Reframe how you read the Fed tile: the tail risk to price is a HIKE, not a delayed cut, and that is asymmetric across this book. A hike scare lifts the long end and the dollar — the classic headwind for 1.6x levered silver and the whole miner complex. The genuinely interesting fact is that gold made a new high anyway, against rising long yields, which is what makes the debasement reading more credible than a rate-cut reading.

items.headline: Empire State hit a four-year high of 20.6 — but the internals are stagflationary, and they corroborate the long-end move
items.summary: Verified line by line against the New York Fed's own August report, downloaded directly after WebFetch returned 403. The file carries an internal generation stamp of 13AUG2026 with public release Monday 17 August 08:30 ET, so the strong reading is genuinely new. Headline general business conditions rose five points to 20.6 from 15.6, 'its highest reading in more than four years'; 97 respondents; responses collected 3-10 August. THE INTERNALS CUT AGAINST THE HEADLINE. Demand SOFTENED: new orders fell to 17.3 from 22.2; shipments fell hard to 11.7 from 24.4. The headline strength came from CONSTRAINT, not demand — unfilled orders jumped to 15.5 and delivery times stretched, while prices paid accelerated and prices received FELL.
items.actionable: This is the cleanest fundamental support for the precious-metals leg in Monday's data: input costs accelerating, supply availability deteriorating and delivery times stretching — all consistent with the Hormuz energy shock feeding through — while firms cannot pass it on. That is a stagflationary print, and it corroborates both the gold breakout and the refusal of the long end to rally. Margin compression at the firm level is the part that eventually reaches equities.

items.headline: OCBC's headline -0.76% is a FALSE ALARM: it went ex-dividend 47 cents Monday, so it actually rose 0.73%
items.summary: Computed in code against the deterministic price feed, which is why it was caught rather than missed. OCBC closed Monday at S$31.55 against Friday's S$31.79 — a headline -0.76%. But its 47-cent interim dividend went ex on Monday 17 August (pay 28 August), so the correct reference is the ex-adjusted 31.32, against which the close represents a genuine RISE of 0.73%. The same trap ran the other way on Friday for DBS: its -1.07% was the S$0.81 ex-dividend (66c quarterly plus a 15c special) almost exactly, meaning the underlying stock was flat rather than down. DBS then rose 1.79% Monday to S$76.88.
items.actionable: If your P&L feed marks OCBC to 31.55 without accruing the 47-cent receivable, the book understates it by about 1.5% until 28 August — and shows a loss on a day the bank gained. Across the two names roughly 2.5% of purely mechanical decline has now passed through in consecutive sessions. The dangerous inverse still applies: if a genuine bank selloff arrives, do not write it off as 'just the dividend'.

items.headline: SETTLED after three attempts: Jackson Hole is 27-29 August. And a date correction — FOMC minutes are THURSDAY 20 Aug 02:00 SGT
items.summary: The Kansas City Fed FAQ returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching, so it was opened in a real browser and read directly. Verbatim: 'The 2026 Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium will take place Aug. 27-29. The topic is Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy.' Dates and theme CONFIRMED; 27-29 August falls Thursday-Saturday, consistent with the traditional format. WARSH: confirmed as Chairman from the Board's own members page. But the KC Fed names NO speakers and posts no 2026 agenda, so whether Warsh speaks is genuinely unknown rather than merely unfound — do not assume the traditional Chair address. DATE CORRECTION: FOMC minutes are Thursday 20 August 02:00 SGT (Wednesday 19 August 14:00 ET). Anyone reading a 'Wednesday' SGT day label would arrive a full day late.
items.actionable: Fix the calendar entry to Thu 20 Aug 02:00 SGT. On content, the minutes cover the 29 July meeting at which three officials dissented FOR a hike, so the market wants to know how close the majority came to joining them and whether September was described as live. The staleness caveat is real: those minutes predate the soft CPI, the soft PPI, the retail-sales miss and the MOU expiry, so they may read hawkish relative to where pricing now sits.
